key_insight: A symbolic, compositional technique lets you quantify how small changes to input features can flip decisions of a decision-tree ensemble, enabling efficient computation of a numeric sensitivity score rather than a simple yes/no vulnerability.
problem_solved: Measures and scales sensitivity analysis for decision-tree ensembles: determining how small perturbations to a subset of features can cause misclassification, in a way that is both quantitative and tractable for large ensembles.
method: Symbolically encode each decision tree's decision regions and how feature perturbations map to classification changes.
Compose per-tree symbolic analyses into an ensemble-level sensitivity metric using algebraic aggregation and bounding to preserve efficiency.
Apply pruning, caching and exact/approximation trade-offs to make computation scalable for real-world ensembles.
impact: Provides practitioners a practical, quantitative robustness measure for tree-based models that supports certification, debugging, and informed mitigation in safety-critical settings.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: input → symbolic encoding of trees → per-tree sensitivity analysis → compositional aggregation to ensemble score
Feature-sensitivity heatmap highlighting which features most influence ensemble instability
Bar/line chart comparing sensitivity scores and computation time versus existing (boolean or sampling) methods
Icon set: certification badge (robustness), shield (safety), magnifying glass (explanation), stopwatch (scalability)
paper_title: Quantifying Sensitivity for Tree Ensembles: A symbolic and compositional approach
paper_authors: S. Akshay, Chaitanya Garg, Ashutosh Gupta, Kuldeep S. Meel, Ajinkya Naik
